nodes.statement: n>=3, kappa>=4, O distributed according to Haar probability on full O(n), and U=O11.
A_O=((kappa+1)/2) I - ((kappa-1)/4)(O+transpose O); singleBlockPrecision must retain exactly this matrix.

nodes.source: A2.SS2.p2.1; standard centered real Gaussian precision formula
nodes.statement: Use the displayed proposed p as a literal real function with sqrt(det A_O), real dimension-half denominator and exp(-quadratic/2). The source calls p_O a density of N(0,A_O^-1); construction, normalization and characterization of that law are not imported by this node.
Finite-dimensional real O(n) is a compact topological group, with the matrix-entry topology and its Borel sigma algebra. Its normalized Haar measure is a finite probability measure.

Matrix entries, finite matrix operations, dot products and determinants are continuous; real sqrt and exp are continuous. With n and kappa fixed, the proposed denominator is a positive constant because 2*pi>0.
For every fixed Euclidean x, O -> det(O)*p(O,WithLp.ofLp x) is continuous on compact O(n), hence genuinely Haar integrable. This needs no spatial majorant or Gaussian-law identification.
For each fixed orthogonal Q, A_(Q O transpose Q)=Q A_O transpose Q.

Orthogonal Q has transpose Q as inverse. Determinant is invariant under conjugation, and quadratic forms satisfy (Qv) dot ((Q A transpose Q)(Qv))=v dot (Av). Thus sqrt determinants and the literal p transform compatibly.
For every fixed Q, O and real coordinate vector v, p(Q O transpose Q,Qv)=p(O,v).
O -> Q O transpose Q preserves full normalized Haar probability and det(Q O transpose Q)=det(O). Background Haar uniqueness/bi-invariance on a compact group justifies the measure assertion.
For each fixed orthogonal Q and vector x, the signed literal Haar average at Qx equals the signed literal Haar average at x, by measure-preserving substitution and integrable kernels.

WithLp.ofLp identifies EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) with real coordinates while preserving the Euclidean inner product as the coordinate dot product. Orthogonal matrix-vector multiplication gives the corresponding Euclidean isometry and commutes with this coordinate identification.

Let j0=0 in Fin n and e be its coordinate basis vector, viewed in EuclideanSpace. Then norm(e)=1, WithLp.ofLp(norm(x) e) is the coordinate vector with value norm(x) at j0 and zero elsewhere, and norm(norm(x) e)=norm(x).

For any Euclidean vectors x,y of equal norm there exists an orthogonal Q with Qx=y. The zero case is valid because norm zero forces both vectors zero; the equal-vector case admits the identity, including x=y=0. The remaining unequal, nonzero case is the usual orthogonal transitivity on a Euclidean sphere. No division by a zero norm or zero difference is allowed.

For every x choose y=norm(x)e. Equal norms and orthogonal transitivity supply a fixed orthogonal Q sending x to this axis vector. The coordinate adapter allows D0 to be applied to its literal coordinate kernel, including x=0.
Integral det(O)*p(O,x) dHaar = integral det(O)*p(O,norm(x)e1) dHaar for every Euclidean x.
e1^T A_O e1=(kappa+1-(kappa-1)U)/2, U=O11. With j0 indexing, (A_O)j0j0=((kappa+1)-(kappa-1)*O_j0_j0)/2; the diagonal of O+transpose O is 2*O_j0_j0.
At v=WithLp.ofLp(norm(x)e), v dot (A_O v)=((kappa+1-(kappa-1)*O_j0_j0)/2)*norm(x)^2. The formula holds for zero radius as well.
p(O,WithLp.ofLp(norm(x)e))=r(O,x), since -quadratic/2 equals -(kappa+1-(kappa-1)*O_j0_j0)*norm(x)^2/4. The sqrt determinant and real dimension-half denominator are unchanged.

For every fixed Euclidean x, O -> det(O)*r(O,x) is continuous on compact O(n), hence genuinely Haar integrable. Equivalently its pointwise equality with the axis p kernel transfers L1. This is separate from spatial integrability.

For every Euclidean x, both signed kernels in the exact proposed signature are Haar integrable and their Haar integrals are equal. The final right-hand side uses the explicit O_j0_j0 exponent r, not only an unspecified radial function or a fixed-Q invariance statement.

exclusions.claim: Actual N(0,A_O^-1) law, density identification, normalization, covariance and probability-measure construction
exclusions.reason: The source introduces p_O as this density, but the accepted target deliberately proves only the literal formula identity. A density-law theorem remains a separate obligation.

exclusions.claim: Spatial integrability, a majorant uniform in O and x, Fubini/Tonelli or any interchange of Haar and Lebesgue integration
exclusions.reason: Fixed-x continuity and compact Haar L1 do not establish these assertions.

exclusions.claim: Ex59 spectral/determinant domination and Ex60 Gaussian spatial integration, H(lambda)
exclusions.reason: These are subsequent source steps outside Ex58 through the immediate axis exponent evaluation.

exclusions.claim: Signed normalization cancellation E15, sphere uniformity and Poisson identities
exclusions.reason: Not dependencies of this literal radialization and coordinate evaluation slice.
